blocks.h2: What Happens When You Call J. Blanton
blocks.intro: A pump you can count on.

img.alt: J. Blanton plumber in shoe covers on a home's front steps with a sewer camera

blocks.body: A battery backup pump sits in the same pit as your main pump and takes over when the power fails or the main pump can't keep up. It's the protection that matters most in Hanover Park, where the 2007 storm brought both heavy rain and outages. Battery systems run for hours depending on the battery and how often the pump cycles. Some homes add a high-water alarm too, so you know right away if something goes wrong.

blocks.h2: Sump Pump Questions From Hanover Park Homeowners

items.q: Do I need a battery backup sump pump?
items.preview: In Hanover Park, it's a good idea.
items.answer: Yes, if you'd like your basement protected when the power goes out. That's what happened in 2007.

items.q: How long do sump pumps last?
How do I test my sump pump?
items.answer: Pour a bucket of water into the pit. The pump should start, empty it and shut off.

items.q: Is a sump pump the same as an ejector pump?
items.answer: No. A sump pump moves groundwater. An [ejector pump](/hanover-park/ejector-pump) moves wastewater.

items.q: How long does a battery backup last?
items.answer: It depends on the battery and how often the pump runs. A strong storm drains it faster.

items.q: Should I replace the main pump and backup together?
items.answer: If both are near the end of their life, replacing them together saves a second visit.

items.q: How much does sump pump repair cost in Hanover Park?
items.preview: It depends on the pump and backup. You'll approve a flat price first.
items.answer: It depends on the pump, the pit and whether you add a backup. You'll approve a flat-rate price before we start.
